subChunks.title: Senior Capstone — Design System
subChunks.hookHtml: This capstone unifies the entire Senior tier: a design system showcase page demonstrating custom @theme tokens, complete CVA component variants, advanced grid layouts, dark mode, container queries, animations, and accessibility — all assembled into a coherent, production-quality design system reference.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Grand Archmage Solomon: "A design system is not a collection of components. It is a set of decisions made once, expressed consistently, understood by everyone, and maintained deliberately. The page you are about to build is not an exercise. It is evidence."

What this capstone builds

A full design system reference page consisting of:

  1. Token Reference Section — colour swatches, spacing scale, typography ramp
  2. Component Gallery — all button variants, badge variants, card variants
  3. Layout Patterns — grid demo, container query demo, sidebar shell
  4. Animation Showcase — entrance animations, loading states, transitions
  5. Dark Mode Toggle — system/light/dark three-state switch

Architecture reminders

/* Token hierarchy */
@theme {
  --color-brand-500: oklch(0.55 0.20 270);
  --color-primary:   var(--color-brand-500);
}

/* Component: CVA + cn() pattern */
const buttonVariants = cva(base, { variants: { variant, size } });
function Button(props) { return <button className={cn(buttonVariants(props))} />; }

/* Grid: auto-fill for responsive, named grid for layouts */
grid-cols-[repeat(auto-fill,minmax(280px,1fr))]

/* Accessibility: every interactive element */
focus:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-2
aria-label or sr-only on icon-only controls

/* Motion: always pair with motion-reduce: */
animate-slide-up motion-reduce:animate-none

/* Container queries: named for clarity */
@container/card ... @md/card:flex-row

The senior's checklist

  • ☐ All interactive elements have keyboard focus styles
  • ☐ Icon-only controls have sr-only labels
  • ☐ All animations have motion-reduce: fallback
  • ☐ Colour tokens used throughout — no raw colours in components
  • ☐ Dark mode tested manually
  • ☐ Container query components verified in narrow context
  • ☐ Grid layouts tested at mobile, tablet, and desktop widths
  • ☐ CSS bundle size checked after build

Solomon: "You are not a senior because you know the utilities. You are a senior because you know when not to use them. Because you ask: 'Is this a semantic token or a one-off?' and 'Is this a container query or a viewport query?' and 'What does motion-reduce need here?' Those questions are the work."

storyBeats.text: The Grand Archmage's study is quiet. The window shows the full Pattern Gardens — every layout you have built, every component you have assembled, every token you have defined, arranged below in their categories. Solomon sits at his desk, not watching.

storyBeats.speaker: Grand Archmage Solomon
storyBeats.text: Build the page. The page is the exam. When you are done, every decision in it should be explainable — not just 'I used this class' but 'I used this class because of this constraint, this pattern, this trade-off.' That is what the level requires.

storyBeats.speaker: Grand Archmage Solomon
storyBeats.text: The token hierarchy. The CVA pattern. The container query architecture. The dark mode three-state system. The animation motion-reduce requirement. The accessibility checklist. These are not separate topics. On this page, they are one system.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a design system showcase page. Apply these classes exactly to the structural elements:

  • .ds-page: min-h-screen, bg-gray-50, dark:bg-gray-950, transition-colors
  • .ds-nav: sticky, top-0, z-50, bg-white/90, dark:bg-gray-900/90, backdrop-blur-md, border-b, border-gray-200, dark:border-gray-800
  • .ds-nav-inner: container, mx-auto, px-4, h-14, flex, items-center, justify-between
  • .ds-section: container, mx-auto, px-4, py-12
  • .ds-section-title: text-2xl, font-bold, text-gray-900, dark:text-white, mb-2
  • .ds-section-desc: text-sm, text-gray-500, dark:text-gray-400, mb-8
  • .ds-grid: grid, grid-cols-[repeat(auto-fill,minmax(280px,1fr))], gap-4
  • .ds-card: bg-white, dark:bg-gray-900, rounded-xl, border, border-gray-200, dark:border-gray-800, p-6, shadow-sm, hover:shadow-md, transition-shadow, animate-fade-in, motion-reduce:animate-none
  • .ds-divider: border-t, border-gray-200, dark:border-gray-800, my-12

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a complete design system reference page from scratch. No class list, no starter code. Requirements: (1) Token reference section with colour swatches and spacing scale. (2) Component gallery with all button and badge variants. (3) A magazine-style 4-column grid with one hero card spanning 2×2. (4) An adaptive container-query card that stacks narrow and rows wide. (5) A three-state dark mode toggle that works via class manipulation on html. (6) All animations paired with motion-reduce: fallback. (7) All interactive elements have visible keyboard focus styles. Demonstrate every pattern from the Senior tier in one cohesive page.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Walk through the architecture decisions on this design system page: why the nav uses bg-white/90 backdrop-blur-md instead of bg-white, why animate-fade-in must be paired with motion-reduce:animate-none, why the grid uses auto-fill minmax instead of fixed grid-cols-3, and why dark mode variants use a class strategy with three states instead of just prefers-color-scheme.

questions.prompt: A design system card grid uses grid-cols-[repeat(auto-fill,minmax(280px,1fr))] gap-4. At 900px viewport width, approximately how many columns appear?
options: 2 columns — auto-fill defaults to 2 columns at 900px
4 columns — 1fr allows cards to shrink below 280px
1 column — auto-fill stacks vertically when the viewport is under 1024px
questions.explanation: auto-fill creates as many columns of at least 280px as fit the container. At 900px: (900 - 2×16) ÷ 280 ≈ 3.1 → 3 columns, each stretching to 1fr of the remaining space. At 560px: (560 - 16) ÷ 280 ≈ 1.9 → 1 column (2 columns would require 560px minimum, too tight). At 600px: 2 columns.

questions.prompt: The sticky nav uses bg-white/90 backdrop-blur-md instead of simply bg-white. A junior asks if this is necessary. What is the correct answer?
options: Yes — bg-white/90 makes the nav semi-transparent, and backdrop-blur-md blurs content behind it, creating the glass morphism effect that signals the nav is floating above content without a hard line
No — bg-white and a border-b are sufficient; backdrop-blur adds GPU cost for purely decorative effect
Both are fine — the choice is purely aesthetic with no functional difference
Yes, but only because dark mode requires the transparency — in light mode, bg-white is preferable
questions.answer: Yes — bg-white/90 makes the nav semi-transparent, and backdrop-blur-md blurs content behind it, creating the glass morphism effect that signals the nav is floating above content without a hard line
questions.explanation: The frosted glass nav is a deliberate UX signal: users can see content scrolling beneath the nav, which confirms they are not at the top of the page. A fully opaque nav creates a hard visual boundary that some designers find abrupt. The backdrop-blur cost (GPU compositing layer) is justified by the pervasiveness of the nav — it is present on every scroll. It is a considered design decision, not a decoration.

questions.prompt: A team reviews the Senior capstone. The card uses animate-fade-in but no motion-reduce: pair. A PR reviewer flags this. What is the correct fix and why?
options: Add motion-reduce:animate-none to the card — users with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce may have vestibular disorders that can be triggered by unnecessary animation
Remove the animation entirely — production components should not have entrance animations
Replace animate-fade-in with opacity-0 and use JavaScript to add opacity-100 after mount
The reviewer is wrong — animate-fade-in is a subtle opacity change that cannot harm any user
questions.answer: Add motion-reduce:animate-none to the card — users with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce may have vestibular disorders that can be triggered by unnecessary animation
questions.explanation: WCAG 2.3.3 (Level AAA) and 2.3.1 (Level A for flashing) require care with animation. Users who set prefers-reduced-motion: reduce often do so because motion causes physical symptoms — not just preference. motion-reduce:animate-none costs one extra class and may prevent a genuine harm. At Senior level, this is not optional — it is a professional standard.
